# Strait of Hormuz Disruptions: The Burden of Oil Price Shocks on Vulnerable Economies

> **Published by:** United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)  
> **Date:** 2 June 2026

---

## Introduction

Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz are sending shockwaves through the global energy market. Vulnerable economies are on the front line: of 75 economies — least developed countries (LDCs) and small island developing States (SIDS) — **65 depend on imported oil**.

For these countries, rising energy prices will translate into higher costs and difficult trade-offs — between covering fuel bills and investing in essential public services. This will affect nearly **1 billion people**.

Without relief, these shocks will further entrench structural inequalities.

> *The analysis is based on 75 vulnerable economies, excluding Singapore from the SIDS group.*

---

## 1. Prices of Oil and Refined Oil Products Have Risen Sharply

![Oil and Gasoline Price Increases](image1.png)

**Price Increases Comparing Pre-crisis (1 Jan 2024 – 27 Feb 2026) vs. Crisis Period (28 Feb – 28 May 2026):**

| Commodity | Price Increase |
|-----------|---------------|
| **Crude oil** | **More than +40%** |
| **Gasoline** | **More than +50%** |

> **Source:** UNCTAD, based on internal data. Crude oil refers to average benchmark prices for Europe (Brent), North America (WTI), Middle East (Dubai), and Russia (Urals). Gasoline refers to average benchmark prices for unleaded gasoline in Europe (Netherlands), North America (United States), and Asia.

---

## 2. Most Vulnerable Economies Are Net Importers of Oil

![Vulnerable Economies Oil Import Dependency](image2.png)

**Key Statistics:**

| Metric | Figure |
|--------|--------|
| **Vulnerable economies analyzed** | 75 |
| **Net oil importers** | **65 out of 75** |
| **LDCs that are net oil importers** | **86%** |
| **SIDS that are net oil importers** | **87%** |
| **People living in these vulnerable economies** | **983 million** |
| **Living below extreme poverty line ($3/day)** | **More than 30%** |

> **Source:** UNCTAD, based on UN Comtrade, UNCTADStat, Asian Development Bank, and World Bank. Latest available data for poverty headcount ratio at $3.00 a day, using 2021 purchasing power parity.

---

## 3. Vulnerable Economies Mainly Import Refined Oil Products

![Crude vs Refined Oil Imports](image3.png)

**Share of Net Imports (2024):**

| Oil Type | Share |
|----------|-------|
| **Crude oil** | **2.2%** |
| **Refined oil products** | **97.8%** |

**Key Finding:** Lacking sufficient refining infrastructure, vulnerable economies mainly import **refined oil products** rather than crude oil. This makes them even more exposed to price shocks, as refined products typically carry a premium over crude oil.

> **Source:** UNCTAD, based on UN Comtrade. Oil products refer to HS 2709 and HS 2710. Figures correspond to the 65 net oil importing vulnerable economies, excluding Singapore.

---

## 4. Additional Cost for Vulnerable Economies: $20.4 Billion Yearly

![Additional Import Bill](image4.png)

**Change in Net Oil Import Bill from a 50% Price Increase (assuming quantities unchanged at 2024 levels):**

| Group | Additional Cost (billion $) |
|-------|---------------------------|
| **Least Developed Countries (LDCs)** | **16.1** |
| **Small Island Developing States (SIDS)** | **4.3** |
| **Total** | **20.4** |

> **Source:** UNCTAD, based on UN Comtrade. Oil products refer to HS 2709 and 2710. Figures for 65 least developed countries and small island developing States that are net importers of crude and refined oil products, excluding Singapore. Seven least developed countries are also small island developing States; they are shown in the LDC aggregate.

## 7. Dependence on Hormuz Region for Oil Supplies

![Hormuz Region Oil Dependence](image7.png)

**Share of Oil Imports Sourced from the Hormuz Region in 2024 (%):**

| Rank | Country | Type | Hormuz Dependence |
|------|---------|------|-------------------|
| 1 | **Seychelles** | SIDS | **99.0%** |
| 2 | **Uganda** | LDC | **61.5%** |
| 3 | **Mauritius** | SIDS | **58.3%** |
| 4 | **United Republic of Tanzania** | LDC | **56.0%** |
| 5 | **Zambia** | LDC | **44.7%** |
| 6 | **Maldives** | SIDS | **43.1%** |
| 7 | **Mauritania** | LDC | **43.0%** |
| 8 | **Mozambique** | LDC | **35.5%** |
| 9 | **Malawi** | LDC | **34.4%** |
| 10 | **Senegal** | LDC | **14.6%** |
| 11 | **Cabo Verde** | SIDS | **12.7%** |
| 12 | **Togo** | LDC | **8.3%** |
| 13 | **Benin** | LDC | **6.5%** |

> **Source:** UNCTAD computations, based on UN Comtrade. Countries sourcing more than 5% of their oil imports from the Hormuz region. Oil products refer to HS 2709 and 2710. Hormuz region considered as Bahrain, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and United Arab Emirates. Net importers excluding Singapore.

**Key Finding:** Seychelles is almost entirely dependent (99%) on the Hormuz region for oil imports, making it exceptionally vulnerable to the disruption. Several LDCs also source more than 40% of their oil from the region.

## 8. Key Considerations

### Increased Cost
Higher oil prices raise freight and fuel costs, increasing the overall cost of goods.

### Broader Inflation
Many vulnerable economies rely heavily on fuel imports, where oil price increases quickly raise the cost of living. Broader inflationary pressures may also affect net oil-exporters.

### Fiscal Pressure
Oil price shocks increase fiscal pressure in net-importing vulnerable economies, forcing trade-offs between:
- Shielding households from price spikes
- Sustaining essential services
- Long-term investment, including for sustainable development

### Economic Slowdown
Increased oil import bills can:
- Widen current account deficits
- Weaken exchange rates
- Trigger higher interest rates
- Tighten credit conditions
- Slow economic growth

**Especially severe in economies with limited fiscal space.**

>
> **— António Guterres**, Secretary-General of the United Nations

## Summary

The military escalation in the Strait of Hormuz has created a severe burden for the world's most vulnerable economies:

| Impact Area | Magnitude |
|------------|-----------|
| **Vulnerable economies affected** | 65 out of 75 |
| **People impacted** | ~983 million |
| **Living in extreme poverty** | >30% |
| **Additional annual import cost** | **$20.4 billion** |
| **LDCs' share of additional cost** | $16.1 billion |
| **SIDS' share of additional cost** | $4.3 billion |
| **Crude oil price increase** | >+40% |
| **Gasoline price increase** | >+50% |
| **Highest GDP impact (LDC)** | Mauritania 7.3% |
| **Highest GDP impact (SIDS)** | Vanuatu 5.8% |
| **Highest Hormuz dependence** | Seychelles 99.0% |

The crisis disproportionately affects countries that:
- Lack refining infrastructure (97.8% import refined products)
- Have limited fiscal space to absorb shocks
- Source a significant share of oil from the Hormuz region
- Already struggle with high poverty rates

Without international relief and support, these oil price shocks will force impossible trade-offs between fuel, food, and essential public services for nearly one billion of the world's most vulnerable people.
